c2_y_prior_art_attack.concept: Active perturbation of CSF/shunt system + response measurement → system identification → failure detection

PMID_26208258.title: Patient Specific Hardware-in-the-Loop Testing of CSF Shunt Systems
what_it_teaches: Real-time hardware-in-the-loop test bed connecting real shunt to mathematical patient model
Model parameters identifiable from standard clinical tests
Accounts for posture-dependent behavior and viscoelastic effects
Simulates infusion tests, cardiovascular modulation, postural changes
24-h test cycle based on recorded patient data
Explicitly envisions development of ACTIVE shunts
what_it_does_NOT_teach: Latent degradation detection from response manifold shift
Failure-mode classification (obstruction vs overdrainage vs fracture vs migration)
Continuous in-vivo perturbation (their system is bench-top, not implantable)
Response-kinetics-based early warning (rise time, recovery time, hysteresis, settling time)

PMID_27203135.title: Physical framework for virtual models of ICP and CSF dynamics in shunt testing
what_it_teaches: Dynamic testing platform reproducing physiological environment
Cardiac/respiratory oscillations, posture changes, cough, sneeze, Valsalva
Hardware+software applying dynamic model-driven pressures to physical shunt

what_is_NOT_known: Continuous in-vivo perturbation-response monitoring (existing work is bench-top)
Longitudinal patient-specific baseline + response-manifold deviation detection
Response-kinetics-based early warning (rise time, recovery, hysteresis, settling)
Latent degradation detection before conventional thresholds
prior_art_assessment.verdict: C2-Y is NOT automatically novel. Perturbation testing is known. The potential novelty is in: (1) continuous in-vivo implementation, (2) longitudinal patient-specific baseline + manifold deviation, (3) response-kinetics analysis, (4) failure-mode classification, (5) latent degradation detection. These must be tested.

H_Y1.hypothesis: Perturbation testing itself is already known.
H_Y1.status: SUPPORTED — PMID 26208258, 27203135 teach dynamic shunt testing with perturbation
H_Y1.implication: C2-Y cannot claim 'perturbation testing for shunt evaluation' as novel

H_Y2.hypothesis: Existing systems can estimate ordinary shunt response but cannot detect patient-specific latent degradation early.
H_Y2.status: PLAUSIBLE — existing systems are bench-top, not in-vivo. They test shunt hardware, not patient-specific degradation over time.
H_Y2.test: Build virtual cohort with longitudinal degradation. Compare perturbation-response baseline vs degraded state. Measure detection lead time vs static pressure threshold.

H_Y3.hypothesis: A longitudinal response-manifold model produces a measurable warning lead-time advantage.
H_Y3.test: Virtual cohort: does response-manifold deviation detect obstruction X days before static pressure threshold?

H_Y4.hypothesis: The response signature can distinguish failure modes better than static monitoring.
H_Y4.test: Virtual cohort with 4 failure modes (obstruction, overdrainage, underdrainage, valve dysfunction). Compare multi-class classification accuracy: static pressure features vs perturbation-response features.

H_Y5.hypothesis: The result is too sensitive to model uncertainty to be clinically useful.
H_Y5.test: Perturb model parameters (compliance, resistance, Starling, sensor) and check if response-manifold classification survives.

c2_y_refined_concept.name: C2-Y1: Active Shunt System Identification for Latent Degradation Detection
c2_y_refined_concept.core_hypothesis: A controlled perturbation-response signature can detect latent degradation before conventional pressure/flow thresholds indicate failure.
c2_y_refined_concept.key_output: Not 'Rshunt = X' but 'The response manifold has shifted by 4.3 SD from this patient's healthy baseline, consistent with early obstruction.'
c2_y_refined_concept.moat: patient-specific baseline → perturbation response library → longitudinal drift model → failure-state classifier
what_must_be_proven: Response-manifold deviation detects degradation BEFORE static pressure threshold (lead-time advantage)
Response signature distinguishes failure modes better than static monitoring
Result survives model uncertainty and sensor drift
c2_y_refined_concept.prior_art_survival: CONDITIONAL — perturbation testing is known, but continuous in-vivo response-manifold tracking for latent degradation is potentially novel. Needs claim-level analysis.

PMID_42508673.title: Mechanics, Fracture, and Fragmentation of Thrombi: A Computational Study Review (2026)
PMID_42508673.finding: Identifies physics-informed digital twins, AI, and virtual patient cohorts as potential routes toward real-time clinical decision support for thrombus fragmentation
PMID_42508673.implication: C5-X direction is scientifically active. Novelty must be specific: validated mechanistic precursor + independent physics + patient-specific twin, not generic 'AI + clot'.
